components.label: Form A — human base mesh (hard-mirrored, retopo'd, verified)
components.description: REBUILT 2026-09-18 as the definitive Form A. Hard-mirrored the ALREADY-retopo'd wip-8 mesh via the measured-midplane-aware symmetrize_mesh(keep='+X') function directly (a true split-and-flip, not the tolerance-gated wrapper) -- residual went from 21.29mm to exactly 0.000mm. Decimate (needed to stay near the 15k budget) is not mirror-aware and reintroduced 0.395mm; re-mirrored a second time AFTER decimate and did not touch face count again, landing at 15558 faces (1.04x budget, accepted). Re-unwrapped UVs each time symmetry was rewritten (both generate_3d's own UV pass and retopo's internal UV pass silently add layers that block a real rewrite -- strip uv_layers before every hard-mirror call). Saved as models/werewolf-wip-9.blend.
components.technique_note: task-config.json's symmetry=mirror_left is NOT wired into rigforge_landmarks.py as of this session (grepped the file -- no task_config/mirror_left/as_designed references at all). Calling rigforge_landmarks(action='prepare') still uses the OLD tolerance-gated logic (skips the rewrite if measured asymmetry is already under the 0.5mm SYMMETRY_TOLERANCE_MM, which is exactly the 'snap' bug the config mode was meant to replace). To get a guaranteed exact 0.000mm hard mirror, call rigforge_landmarks.measure_symmetry() + rigforge_landmarks.symmetrize_mesh(obj, midplane, keep='+X') directly via the module (bypassing prepare_for_rigging's tolerance gate) -- this is what actually worked. Worth fixing at the tool level in a future pass so 'hard-mirror' doesn't require reaching around the wrapper.

echo_renders.honest_read: Confirmed: arms run down the sleeve centerline, legs and spine centered, both views clean by eye.

weight_maps_2026_09_18.honest_read: Both maps are clean and tightly localized to their own limb with a smooth falloff -- no visible leakage onto the torso or adjacent limb in either image. This does NOT show the breast<->pelvis overlap finding below, since neither breast nor pelvis was one of the two bones rendered.

tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.finding: Ran (confirmed via direct rigforge_skin(action='apply') call, which matched the auto-embedded result almost exactly) but did NOT reach 0.000 overlap on this character, contrary to the commit message's 'werewolf: stray 4.351->0.000' example. Measured: stray_mass 91.86, verdict fail, 8 outlier pairs, worst = 320 vertices shared between DEF-breast.L and DEF-pelvis.R (382mm apart).
tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.root_cause: Tag-constrained skinning only blocks CROSS-tag weight leakage. This character's 'Torso' tag is one bucket covering 13 bones (both breast bones, both pelvis bones, and the full spine chain) -- breast and pelvis are BOTH legal for any Torso-tagged vertex, so bone-heat weight bleeding between them (they are anatomically 382mm apart but topologically close across a thin jacket+jeans mesh) is allowed by the rule and untouched by the constraint. This is a real, reproducible measurement, not a bug in how the tool was called -- re-running rigforge_skin directly reproduced the same number. A finer tag split (e.g. separate Chest/Pelvis tags within Torso) would likely fix it but was not attempted this round -- it is a bigger tagging change than 'apply the new default'.
tag_constrained_skinning_2026_09_18.reported_honestly: The artist was told the real number (91.86, not 0.000) rather than the commit's example, with the mechanism explained.

override.why: Explicit instruction this turn to continue skin -> correctives -> animate -> stop before export, with a stop-and-report condition only on skin, not on correctives. Correctives authored 10 JCM shape keys and is a documented partial recovery (knees ~20%->9.9% at max flex, elbows only 52.4%->47.7% because the harness's volume metric is a convex hull and only the pinched side can be pushed back, head has a known 35.3mm skinning/Blender-eval mismatch from a non-vertex-group deformer). Further improvement needs a targeted re-weight (fix ladder rung 2), out of scope for this turn; proceeding to animate as directed.
